exposure: leaving the placenta in situ (LPIS) management for placenta accreta spectrum (PAS)
outcome: longitudinal changes in uterine artery (UtA) Doppler velocimetry (peak systolic velocity (PSV), end-diastolic velocity (EDV), and pulsatility index (PI))
cohort: The study included 34 patients with placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) managed by leaving the placenta in situ (LPIS) postpartum.
finding: In patients with placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) managed by leaving the placenta in situ (LPIS), mean uterine artery (mUtA) pulsatility index (PI) is markedly lower in the first 8 weeks postpartum compared to patients without PAS, and UtA Doppler indices show significant changes at or after 8 weeks postpartum, characterized by an increase in mUtA PI and a reduction in mUtA PSV and EDV compared to predelivery values.
